espn-603993.headline: Argentina reach Dublin 109 caps lighter than planned
beats: Santiago Carreras, 70 Tests, hurt his leg in the Prem. Thomas Gallo, 39 caps, dislocated a wrist and is out for at least six months. Their places go to Mateo Soler, whose Test debut came off the bench against Australia in September, and Rodrigo Martinez, a loosehead with four caps.

Argentina have not won since beating Wales 35–21 in July. Two home games against Australia since then brought a defeat and a 28–28 draw. Ireland's last Test was a 40–21 loss to New Zealand, so nobody arrives on a run.
Ireland may have a prop question of their own. Tadhg Furlong has been cited over an alleged groin grab in Leinster's win over Munster.
Win by 16 or more and Argentina go above Australia in the world rankings. Two home games against Australia could not manage that.

espn-603994.headline: Erasmus can afford to lose players, not this game
beats: Cheslin Kolbe is out for the rest of the Nations Championship with a broken jaw. André Esterhuizen limped off in Cardiff after barely a minute, and Handré Pollard is in doubt. South Africa lead the table on points difference alone, level with New Zealand on 15.

Italy have not played since July, when they conceded 47 to New Zealand and 57 to Australia a week apart. Their last win was 23–18 over England in March. The last meeting, in Italy in November 2025, finished 14–32.
Sir Graham Henry admires Erasmus for being willing to lose matches to improve the side. An Italian win would cost him first place in the world, to New Zealand.
South Africa play France away six days later, which is no place for a new combination to be learning its lines.

sources.title: Crocked Boks a blessing in disguise
Sir Graham Henry: Why I admire Rassie Erasmus who is prepared to lose

espn-603995.headline: New Zealand bring 14 tries to Scotland's open house
beats: New Zealand scored seven tries in each of their October wins over Australia, 50–19 and 43–21. That was their answer to three straight defeats by South Africa.
Scotland score freely too, with seven tries apiece against France and Argentina. They also conceded 40 and 38 in those wins, and 42 against South Africa. Their games are rarely tidy.
The last meeting, at Murrayfield in November 2025, ended Scotland 17–25 New Zealand. Holding this attack to 25 again would be a start. Win, and Scotland go above England into fifth in the world.
The two meet again in Dunedin before next year's World Cup, Scotland's first Test in New Zealand in 27 years. The last one, at Eden Park in 2000, finished 48–14.

espn-603996.headline: Last year a point split them. Japan now sit above
beats: Wales won 24–23 in Cardiff on 15 November 2025. Japan come back ranked ninth in the world, two places above their hosts.
Japan beat Fiji 20–15 for the Pacific Nations Cup in September. Fiji won the rematch 34–28 on 24 October and spoiled the Japanese union's centenary doing it.

Wales last played on 18 July and lost 0–43 in South Africa without a try. Dillon Lewis started that game and all three before it, his first Tests after two years out of the squad. He has 60 caps and has kept his place in Steve Tandy's squad for November.
Win, by any margin, and Wales go above Japan into ninth. Last November one point was enough.

espn-603997.headline: France's absentee list reaches eleven before Fiji
beats: France were already without Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos. Then fly-half Antoine Hastoy hurt his ankle in the Top 14, and his replacement in the squad is Castres fly-half Louis Le Brun, who has no caps. That makes eleven players gone from Fabien Galthié's plans before a ball is kicked.

Fiji are bottom of the Nations Championship with no points, and conceded 73 to England at home in July. Jake White's first game in charge was a 34–28 win over Eddie Jones' Japan in Tokyo, against the side that beat them in the Pacific Nations Cup final a month earlier.
France beat Fiji 34–21 at home in November 2025. Lose this one and they drop out of the top four, with South Africa waiting at the Stade de France six days later.
Galthié would rather meet them with fewer names on the list.

espn-603998.headline: England have three spare 10s and want the first one
beats: Fin Smith started at fly-half in all three of England's July Tests. He then damaged a calf for Northampton against Leicester and missed the Bagshot camp. England say they remain hopeful, and Borthwick has called up Charlie Atkinson anyway, alongside Marcus Smith and George Ford.

Whoever wears 10 faces a defence that conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October, three weeks after beating South Africa 42–38. Their last meeting, at home for England in November 2025, finished 25–7.
A misfiring England backline matters more than usual. Lose, and England drop from fifth to seventh in the world, below Australia and Scotland.
Japan come to England the following week. That is a gentler place to bed in a fly-half.

sources.title: England fret over Fin Smith’s fitness for looming Australia match
